(b) Passing checks carried no expected value, so a comparison could not match a check that changed between right and wrong; earlier "0 regressions" counts were not a valid test.
experiments.success: Every run re-scored with the corrected scorer before any verdict; comparisons refuse scores without stable check ids.

experiments.examples: certification found: 234 of 287 under education; issuer read 0 of 234

experiments.title: Names printed over two or three lines
experiments.failureClass: IDENTITY_UNRESOLVED refusals: 48 of 300 CV documents refused (6 Word, 10 PDF, 11 scan, 21 photo), so the applicant would never appear in the list
experiments.hypothesis: Designs that print the first name over the surname, or an oversized surname first, defeat the one-line name rule; joining consecutive single-word lines confirmed by the e-mail's local part recovers them without turning headings into names.
experiments.success: Fewer CV refusals on the protected split; every newly published name correct.
experiments.reject: any new wrong name; any check from right to wrong in any format; unexplained golden-output change
experiments.tests: test/parser-split-names.test.ts (3 failed before; 2 counterexamples and 1 unchanged case)
experiments.cost: no measurable runtime change (median per document unchanged; same OCR)
experiments.examples: CV0507 "Tumelo / DAVIDS" → Tumelo Davids; CV0517 "Smith / Jessica" with jessicasmith.517@… → Jessica Smith (development examples)
experiments.decision: Demonstrated improvement within the evaluated scope
experiments.decisionNote: Protected: CV documents published 112 → 119 of 135, all 7 with the right name; wrong names unchanged at 3. Remaining protected refusals: 16 (10 of them photos). Reproduced exactly from the clean commit (e1-r1 against the earlier uncommitted run: no difference).
experiments.decisionOwner: assistant, within the evaluated scope (production promotion is the owner's)

Re-computed with 2.0.0: 0 right → wrong, 0 correct checks removed; 7 documents refused → published, adding 169 correct and 103 erroneous checks of their own (the published documents' remaining field errors).

experiments.title: " / " separates skill-list items
experiments.failureClass: skill recall 64 of 376 (Word) at baseline: slash-separated skill lists were judged to be prose and dropped; the few skills shown came from a dictionary fallback, which also renamed them
experiments.hypothesis: Treating a spaced slash as a list separator (and keeping a slash inside a name such as CI/CD) recovers listed skills.
experiments.success: Higher skill recall on the protected split; printed-skill precision not more than 2 points lower; unsupported skill names not increased; no check from right to wrong.
experiments.reject: any of: precision down more than 2 points; unsupported skill names up; any right-to-wrong check; unexplained golden-output change
experiments.tests: test/parser-slash-skills.test.ts (3 failed before; counterexample: CI/CD, TCP/IP and UI/UX read exactly as in a comma list)
experiments.examples: "Ticketing / Troubleshooting / Windows / …" now gives all eight skills; new unsupported names on protected photos are OCR fragments ("Pro tection")
experiments.decision: Failed a gate; retained for investigation
experiments.decisionNote: Owner decision: not promoted. Isolated behind PARSER_EXPERIMENTS=E2 (commit 228852a); the default is again parser 2.9.0. Superseded measurement: "579 gains, 0 regressions" came from comparator 1.1.0, which ignored checks present in one run only; comparator 2.0.0 (tested) gives, protected split against the accepted default: 579 skill recalls wrong → right, 579 precision checks added correct, 35 errors added and 42 removed (unsupported names: photos +2, scans +1/−1, Word and text −4 each).
experiments.downstream: no new unjustified credit at leaf level in any format; under-credit against verified inputs recovered: Word and text 669 each, PDF 563, scan 515, photo 327 (matching-a-default-r1_b-e2-r2_c-e3-r1.json)

experiments.title: Admission check for skill-list pieces (on top of E2)
experiments.component: parser–reading interface: admission of list pieces
experiments.failureClass: E2 admits every " / " piece as a skill. On OCR'd photos and scans, column interleaving puts prose and fragments from another column into the skills block ("Recent responsibilities include tracking", "am", "and", "improvement"), and wrapped items arrive split ("Root cause" / "analysis").
experiments.rootCauseEvidence: development (inspected) documents 04_Phone_Photo_PDF CV0503, CV0524, CV0541, CV0549: OCR text shows " | " column boundaries inside slash lists and profile prose interleaved line by line.
experiments.hypothesis: Most E2 false positives are list pieces that are not complete items: they begin or end with a function word, or come from the far side of a column boundary (" | " inside a " / " list) and are prose-like. Refusing those pieces keeps E2's recall.
experiments.intervention: ONE factor, admission only: (1) a listed piece that begins or ends with a function word (and, or, for, the, of, to, with, across, am, is, are, have, has, include, includes, including), or is only function words, is not admitted; (2) in a line whose items are separated by " / " and that also contains " | ", the bar is a column boundary, and a bar-segment containing no " / " is admitted only if it is at most 3 words, does not start with a lower-case letter, and passes (1). Splitting, wrap-joining and normalisation are unchanged.
experiments.success: Measured A (accepted default 2.9.0), B (E2), C (E2+E3) on the same inputs, on the validation split v2 (13 candidates) and on development v2 separately, per format AND in total: unsupported skill names in C ≤ A in every format and in total (E2's original gate, unchanged); C's skill-recall gain over A ≥ 90% of B's gain in every format; extra-printed skill errors C ≤ B in every format; no right → wrong check outside skills against A; median runtime per format ≤ B + 10%; golden outputs unchanged.
experiments.reject: any success condition not met. Validation v2 is not fresh: even a pass permits no promotion; promotion evaluation is blocked until a new batch.
experiments.budget: 3 full batch runs (about 5 minutes each), no downloads, no training
experiments.cost: median per document unchanged or lower than B (photo 2,400 → 2,245 ms on development); no downloads; three batch runs
experiments.examples: development CV0503 (PDF, scan): "Attention to detail" lost because the filtered line became prose; CV0522 scan: "Data day delivery" admitted; CV0530 photo: "Supplier coordination coordination" admitted, alongside six real skills recovered
experiments.decisionNote: Validation gates met only vacuously (C identical to B there). On development, where the mechanism exists, unsupported names stay above A on photos and scans and two correct skills are lost: the column filter changed the prose-or-list classification, an unintended second factor. Code kept off behind PARSER_EXPERIMENTS=E3 for reproducibility; the next experiment targets reading order (E4).
experiments.downstream: matching-a-default-r1_b-e2-r2_c-e3-r1.json: no new unjustified credit in any format; 33 more under-credited criterion leaves recovered on photos

modelExperiments.component: evidence assessment (Formula A leaves); OCR and parser fixed at 2.9.0
modelExperiments.hypothesis: A pretrained local instruct model applying the written rubric to the same passages assesses requirement leaves more accurately than the rules baseline on negation, wishes, contradictions, title-only roles, weak use and transfer gating, without more unsupported positive assessments.
candidates: B: qwen3:4b-instruct-2507-q4_K_M (installed, Apache-2.0, 2.5 GB, Ollama 0.35.1, temperature 0, seed 0)
B8: qwen3:8b (installed, Apache-2.0, 5.2 GB): the ONLY changed factor is the model; prompt and rubric identical
modelExperiments.dataset: server/test/assessment/evidence/annotations-v0.1.jsonl (47 items, 11 categories; sha256 5d6d348a9c1fa0e9…); evaluation split 21 items reserved by stratified hash before any model run; development 26
modelExperiments.labels: proposed by the assistant, NOT independent; every result is provisional until a person reviews the labels
metrics: state agreement per category and overall
unsupported positive assessments (more credit than the label)
relevant evidence missed (less credit than the label)
evidence-reference correctness (cited support overlaps the label's support)
consequential differences (credit gap of at least 0.5)
latency median and maximum per leaf
modelExperiments.acceptance: On the evaluation split, for B to count as better than A WITHIN THIS SET: unsupported positives B ≤ A; state agreement B ≥ A + 3 items; repeatability 100% identical states; validator refusals ≤ 10% of items; maximum latency ≤ 10 s per leaf. Passing supports only a provisional, unreviewed-label claim: no promotion, no integration.
modelExperiments.resources: no downloads (both models installed); about 47 × 4 model calls; no training
modelExperiments.decision: Failed its pre-registered agreement gate against unreviewed proposed labels; not eligible for promotion
modelExperiments.results: Evaluation split, 21 items, labels unreviewed. A rules: 14 of 21 states agree; 5 unsupported positives (two negations and one wish credited as named; a contradiction credited as named; a title-only role counted relevant); 2 missed; 6 consequential. B qwen3 4B: 15 of 21; 1 unsupported positive ("reconciled customer accounts" read as customer service); 2 missed (abstained on a clear negation; abstained on a wish next to shown use); 2 consequential; 21 of 21 repeatable; 0 refusals; 4.6 s median and 5.7 s maximum per leaf. B8 qwen3 8B: 11 of 21; 1 unsupported positive; 7 missed (named, course, transfer and described evidence answered as no evidence); 6 consequential; maximum 10.8 s per leaf.

runs.verdict: INVALID (integration defect, not a model result)
runs.why: the runtime schema offered abstain as a nullable enum and the constrained decoder never chose null, so both models' states were overridden as abstentions (8B abstained on 46 of 47 items); the 4B model's long rationales failed the 400-character schema check (26 refusals). Diagnosed on a development item only. Rules baseline unaffected: evaluation agreement 14 of 21.

modelExperiments.harnessFix: answer schema 0.2.0: explicit "none" for abstain, mapped back to null; rationale length enforced while generating (maxLength 300). Prompt text and rubric unchanged (evidence-prompt-0.1.0, evidence-rubric-0.1.0).
modelExperiments.decisionOwner: assistant, against the pre-registered gates (the owner may overrule)
modelExperiments.decisionNote: B needed at least 3 more agreeing states than the rules on the evaluation split and achieved 1 more; B8 failed agreement and latency. Not reinterpreted. Reduced false credit (1 unsupported positive against 5; 2 consequential against 6) is a promising exploratory finding, not independently verified improvement. No training, no prompt tuning.

defectInvestigations.title: Upload latency after portal reservations
defectInvestigations.symptom: 12 concurrent uploads: ~14 s warm at baseline, 15-16 s after; 4 s unrelated-request gate failing at a pool of 3
defectInvestigations.hypothesis: H1: wall time scales with database statements per document through a small connection pool; reservation and release added ~2 of ~14
defectInvestigations.change: merge usageOf's three queries into one statement (reservation logic untouched)
defectInvestigations.result: acquisitions per document 14 -> 11.4-12.3; upload request 25% faster than baseline; pool of 10: current faster than baseline; pool of 3: gate still failing 4 of 5
defectInvestigations.decision: accepted the change; gate retained unchanged and failing at a pool of 3; residual unexplained; H3 untested
